Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Brad Wilcox
Message:
feat(robustness): trim DSN whitespace + fail fast on source-map misconfiguration (v0.1.1) (#4)

- JS: clientDsn()/serverDsn() now call .trim() on env vars so surrounding
  whitespace cannot fool the enabled-gate or reach Sentry.init with a dirty DSN
- JS: withAaaSentry() throws a clear build-time Error when SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is
  set but SENTRY_ORG or SENTRY_PROJECT is missing, turning a silent misconfiguration
  into an immediate failure
- Python: init_sentry() already stripped SENTRY_DSN; no source change needed
- Tests: 17 new vitest cases (DSN trim + config-time validation for all three
  init functions and withAaaSentry) and 5 new pytest cases (DSN trim + no-op paths)
- Version bumped to 0.1.1 in package.json and python/pyproject.toml

Author: Brad Wilcox
Message:
feat(scrubber): harden to general-purpose secret/PII scrubber (#2)

Expands the JS + Python scrubbers from email + UUID-only to a
comprehensive four-layer scrubber: (1) Bearer tokens, (2) 19 secret
param key names matched by word boundary with value redaction,
(3) email addresses, (4) UUID-v4 / token-like patterns.  `authorization`
is deliberately absent from the key-name list — the Bearer rule handles
it end-to-end without stripping the word "Bearer" from the output.
Placeholder names updated to [REDACTED_EMAIL] / [REDACTED_TOKEN] /
[REDACTED].  Exports BEARER_RE + SECRET_KEY_RE alongside existing names.
Both test suites extended with non-UUID-value fixture cases, Bearer
assertions, and non-secret-param survival checks (36 JS / 35 Python,
all green).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
